# 07 Resolve nested control-flow blocks into the SequenceModel

## Outcome

`buildSequenceModel` assigns block ids (`${kind}-${n}`, 1-based per kind in document order),
validates every participant id referenced anywhere inside a block's body (recursively) against
the explicit-reference rule, and computes each block's recursive participant-touch set (the set
of participant ids referenced anywhere in its body, including nested blocks) — the input
`layoutSequence` needs in ticket 08 to compute each block's horizontal extent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `loop` node resolves with a stable `loop-1` id (and `loop-2` for a second top-level loop,
  etc.), matching the auto-id convention.
- [ ] `alt`/`par`/`critical` branch labels pass through unchanged; each branch's body resolves
  its own statements independently.
- [ ] A block's `participantsTouched` set includes every participant referenced by any message
  directly in its body, plus every participant touched by any nested block in its body
  (recursive union) — verified with a three-level-nested fixture (`loop` > `alt` > `par`).
- [ ] A message inside a block referencing an undeclared participant produces the same error
  diagnostic as a top-level message would (reuses ticket 02's explicit-reference validation,
  applied recursively).
- [ ] `rect`'s color string passes through unvalidated (rendering ticket 09's concern, not
  build's).

## Test seam

`buildSequenceModel(document: SequenceDocument): { model: SequenceModel | null; diagnostics:
Diagnostic[] }` — unit level, pure function, hand-built fixtures (does not require ticket 06's
real parser).
